mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 3% for two consecutive months triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0 and remains above 3.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average during similar inflation spikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS labor cost growth above 2% for three consecutive months signals wage stickiness and upward price pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: During analogous labor-cost acceleration regimes, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative in >70% of instances (empirical robustness test).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST industrial production and RSAFS retail sales by at least 2% in the same month predicts a near-term demand contraction, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous_month and RSAFS < previous_month by ≥2%
failure_condition: During comparable dual-industry contraction episodes, the 5-day forward return is not statistically different from the mean of prior contraction periods (Granger causality p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in monthly INDPRO supply index below 100 (from ≥105) coincides with a rise in FEDFUNDS, creating supply-side uncertainty that produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In analogous dual-signal episodes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in UNRATE unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months, in the context of FEDFUNDS < 4%, signals a disinflationary policy stance that supports equity risk appetite over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 4.0
failure_condition: During similar policy regimes, 60-day forward returns do not exceed the 5th percentile of prior low-rate periods (out-of-sample quantile test).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly PAYEMS exceeding 4% in a single month, without preceding acceleration, predicts short-term wage inflation fears and a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In analogous isolated spikes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (robustness across 10 such events).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of GDP deflator inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% and a decline in monthly GDPC1 demand index by ≥3% forecast a demand-supply mismatch that drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.5 and GDPC1 < previous month by ≥3%
failure_condition: During similar dual-signal episodes, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from baseline (Granger causality p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of FEDFUNDS above 5.25% for 4 consecutive months creates a risk premium for safe assets, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days in a non-recessionary economy.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5.25 for four consecutive months AND RSI^GDP < 50 (non-recessionary signal)
failure_condition: During analogous high-rate periods in non-recessionary regimes, 60-day forward returns are not persistently negative (rolling quantile test).
